title: Diagnosis of Respiratory Distress Syndrome and Transient Tachypnea in Newborns
author: Marconi Augusto Aguiar dos Reis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbsninde

steps.title: Diagnose Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN)
steps.instruction: Identify TTN based on clinical characteristics and radiographic findings, ensuring extrapulmonary conditions are excluded.

substeps.instruction: Confirm tachypnea persists after 2 hours of life with mild respiratory distress (refer to Silverman Anderson Bulletin if possible).
Observe for self-limited tachypnea that may worsen up to 24-48 hours and typically resolves by 72 hours or up to the 5th day of life.
Exclude newborns with diagnosed extrapulmonary conditions causing tachypnea, such as infection, cardiological, neurological, or metabolic diseases.

Perform chest radiography to identify diffuse interstitial infiltrate distributed from the hilum, thickening of the lobar fissure, or opacity by perihilar reinforcement (mild to moderate cardiomegaly may be present).
Note that IUGR and lack of antenatal corticosteroids for fetal maturation (ACFM) increase the likelihood of TTN over RDS.

steps.title: Diagnose Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
steps.instruction: Identify RDS based on the onset of tachypnea, radiographic evidence of surfactant deficiency, and oxygenation requirements.

substeps.instruction: Identify onset of tachypnea in the first hours of life, worsening within 24 hours, and an increasing need for ventilatory support.

Perform chest X-ray in the first 24 hours of life (or before surfactant administration) to check for granular opacity, diffuse pulmonary reticulo-granular infiltrate (ground-glass appearance), reduced lung volume, and air bronchograms.
Monitor saturimetry; identify levels below 92-95% with progressive worsening and a requirement for FiO2 above 35-45% to maintain PO2 > 50mmHg.
Assess blood gas for compatibility with progressive pulmonary insufficiency.
Observe for clinical improvement following surfactant administration.
Note that maternal diabetes mellitus and absence of ACFM increase the possibility of RDS.

steps.title: Confirm Diagnosis via Expert Review
steps.instruction: Have two neonatology experts review medical records to confirm the diagnosis of RDS and TTN.

substeps.instruction: Review X-rays, laboratory assessments, and clinical evolution.
Exclude other causes of ventilatory support, specifically sepsis, meconium aspiration syndrome, and birth with acidosis.
